generated_from: origin/main at campaign start; focused Windows and Linux x86-64 WSL validation

capabilities.scope: Static string operations coexist with owned UTF-8 text and byte buffers. Runtime text length is byte-based; no general Unicode code-point or grapheme API is claimed.
capabilities.caveat: The campaign executed byte-length text operations in the CSV parser and Pebble compiler on Linux x86-64. General Unicode scalar/grapheme processing remains outside the contract; the Assembly emulator lacks dynamic text built-ins.

capabilities.scope: Closed bytes family with explicit capacity, checked access, reserve, push, clone, concat, slice, and text conversion; no generic Buffer<T> or implicit growth.
capabilities.caveat: Hosted IR and Linux x86-64 native O0/O1 execution passed for byte-oriented encoding and compiler workloads. The Assembly emulator does not provide the dynamic collection built-ins used by these workloads.

capabilities.scope: Owned UTF-8 text supports explicit construction/capacity and text operations; UTF-8 byte length and bounded allocation are part of the contract.
capabilities.caveat: CSV parsing and the Pebble compiler exercised byte-length text conversion natively at O0/O1. General-purpose formatting/locale APIs and arbitrary Unicode scalar iteration are not established. The Assembly emulator lacks text/vector builtin execution.

capabilities.scope: S3 code can process bounded bytes/text and the experimental substrate contains source-derived lexer/parser slices. A general mature parser library or unrestricted text runtime is not present.
capabilities.caveat: The experimental parser is a bounded subset; it is not the production compiler frontend and does not establish a general source-language parser package.

capabilities.scope: Programs have explicit opaque host_capability/resource_handle operations. Providers are injected at the embedding boundary; the source API is not a general path/open/read/write filesystem API.
capabilities.caveat: Hosted provider lifecycle is tested with provider fixtures. The native provider is deterministic and does not access real files, processes, or sockets.

capabilities.scope: Closed tryte_vector, i64_vector, and f64_vector families with explicit capacity and deterministic operations; not arbitrary vector<T> syntax.
capabilities.caveat: The campaign ran hosted IR and Linux x86-64 native O0/O1 vector workloads. The Assembly emulator rejects dynamic vector built-ins rather than providing matching execution.

capabilities.scope: Deterministic closed families include i64_map, i64_set and text_i64_map; ordering is explicit and lookup is bounded by collection length.
capabilities.caveat: The word generic in some milestone names does not mean arbitrary source-level key/value type constructors.

capabilities.scope: There is no general user-defined vector<T>/map<K,V>/set<T> facility; implemented collection families are closed and type-specific.
Typed shared/mutable references and bounded slices have provenance, borrow checks, indexing, and source/native ABI contracts.
capabilities.caveat: Native execution gates are platform-specific and were not run on this Windows host.

capabilities.scope: Hosted tests cover dynamic owners in records, enum payloads, fixed arrays of records, replacement and move/borrow rejection. Arbitrary dynamic collections of owned aggregates remain outside the closed design.
capabilities.caveat: The two M1.51 documents still describe implementation as not started, contradicting current executable tests; native composite-owner execution was not evaluated in this campaign.

capabilities.scope: The normal compiler resolves explicit imports/exports, transitive dependencies, aliases, nominal identities and deterministic source ordering. Native module execution is available subject to platform validation.
Recoverable domain failures can use declared nominal result enums and explicit exhaustive match/return. There is no generic Result<T,E>, exception unwinding, or implicit propagation.
C exports/imports and scalar plus borrowed-slice boundaries are present. Owned S3 dynamic aggregates do not cross C; actual shared-library execution requires the native host/toolchain.
capabilities.caveat: This campaign ran hosted/code-generation assertions only where Linux-native execution was skipped on Windows.

capabilities.scope: Capability-scoped provider registry and deterministic opaque handles exist. Provider implementations are host supplied; current native fixture is not a real OS provider.

docs/structured-data-capabilities.md predates later source-level records/enums/owned text; it says records/enums are unsupported and strings are reserved. Current tests and later ADRs prove portions of those capabilities exist. Treat that inventory as historical, not current truth.
